stoppedItems: ok: none has come back. (1) Larry never sings or hums, no band member remarks on a note, there is no music at the table, and nobody finishes the busker's tune. (2) No tag sets Larry against a maker: after the busker he says only `good-one`, `started-anyway` and `never-ends`, all three about the singer. (3) He is without an answer twice (`no-joke` with `i-looked`, and `dont-know`) and names no job either time. (4) The busker's syllable is 'la', uncaptioned (`busker-tune`, `busker-behind`). (5) Nothing is sung at the table or at the close; `busker-behind` is the same wordless phrase on the street and has no words to change.
lookedAtAndPassed: (1) `started-without-me` then `late`, with `counted-in`: Larry counts himself out and a flat line from the house counts him in, a minute before the goodnight. Both aired episodes ended with the house taking him in after he had put himself outside it (the pilot: his sung wish and 'You are in it.'; 002-2026-w47: 'I only host.', one unsure note, 'We can work with that.', the key change), and the ledger lists the song stopping to take the host in as aired twice. Passed, because every part of that device is absent: no song, no stop, no lights down or up, he does not sing, nothing of his is corrected or fitted, no hook changes a word; and because the ledger's own entry classes the host left out or small as the character with its lines done, and this is a new particular in which he is simply wrong. It is still the same arc of feeling a third time running, and it rests on one line added at assembly that no gate had seen. See forTheOwner. (2) Cue `they-look`, `chair`, cue `chair-in`: every head turned to one party, 1.3 s of stillness, a band member's flat word, the room back warmer. The aired song's ending had every head in the band turned to the desk, a wait of the same length, Hy's flat line, every bulb on, and then the band turning to the lens. Passed at select by both reviewers and passed again: there the look waited for the host's note and the acceptance was the music changing to fit it; here it is a stranger in a doorway, the acceptance is a piece of furniture, and what follows is an argument about a bowl. It stays clear only if it is staged as a look and not as a stop. (3) Cue `tune-stops`, cue `coin`, `never-ends`: a tune that stops wanting one more note, a held silence, and Larry putting something small into it. The aired vamp stopped on a chord that wanted one more note and Larry sang into the silence. Passed: there the gap was the cue for his note and the band then made it right; here nobody fills it, the singer starts again, and the tune staying unfinished is the picture the crossing's sentence answers. It stays clear only if the coin is heard as a coin. (4) `come-up`, and Larry speaking to the camera as a visitor throughout: the aired making-of had him keep a host's manners toward his own camera as it went in. The companion camera is the owner's outline, and 'Come on up.' is a different phrase doing a plain job with no joke in it. (5) The say-back device against the aired 'A member asked:' (the host voicing an absent person's question as the set-up of an answer): the owner's device, staged as listening, with no formula of attribution. (6) `zhuangzi-name` against the show's two jokes on its own voice (a word the engine could not say; a word the tool misheard): a reader's hedge inside the fiction, with no panel, label or picture. (7) `no-joke`, `i-looked`, `dont-know`, `guest-in-sentence` against 'I only host.' and 'I'm not in it.': none names what he is or finds him missing, and the last puts him inside the sentence by courtesy and plants the word that the door and the table then use. (8) Cue `scarf-on` against the pilot's tuxedo drawing itself on: the owner's stage direction done without hands, in silence, with the cut to the collar still open to the builder. The gold scarf and the gold chair against gold carrying a punch twice in 002-2026-w47: a marker by the cast chapter's rule, and no line points at it. (9) `rule`, `still-the-rule`, `ruling-stands`, `chair`, `counted-in`, `long-way`: Sibyl ruling, Eppy calling a ruling, one word from Al, a drummer's complaint and a bandleader a step ahead are natures with new content; Pete has not spoken alone on air before. `my-house`: Larry losing in his own home is the character with a new defeat. (10) Cue `watch-the-cook` and cue `cross` against the aired wordless stretches: 2.4 s and 5 s, nothing demonstrated in use, and the joke chapter now holds the technique as craft. (11) The owner's lines are not judged. For the record, 'Oh, no show tonight, folks.' mirrors the pilot host's first words ('Oh. Oh no. We're on.'), and a goodnight with a word for the audience is a form the ledger calls spent. (12) The opening and the close against both aired episodes: see reason. The stock end card is not in the script; if it runs, the special ends on the studio wide and the credits as both aired episodes did.
reason: Nothing in its lines, devices, images, sounds, opening or close does a job an aired episode did, and none of the five stopped items is in it. It opens on a switched-off studio with no announcer, no title line and no audience (the pilot opened on black with an invented post and an announce formula; 002-2026-w47 on a pen plotter with the announcer naming the host), and it closes on the owner's three lines from a chair at a table, a hold and a fade (the pilot: a key press and a collapsing picture; 002-2026-w47: a song, a toast, the widest shot under long applause). There is no song, card, stamp, label, count or reaction sound in it. What comes nearest the record is the last minute, where the house is fonder of Larry than he expects and then makes room for the viewer. I judge that by mechanism and pass it: the feeling is the outline's, and the device that aired twice (the music stopping, the lights, his note, a changed word) is not here in any part. Two items stay clear only if they are staged as written; both are in lookedAtAndPassed and forTheOwner.
retell: The one where there's no show, so Larry walks you home through the cold, tells you at a red light on an empty road that an old rabbi said we don't have to finish the work and don't get to quit, and then can't leave you on the pavement outside his own dinner.
evidence: Read once through as a viewer, then against the count: 397 spoken words and 11 sung syllables, 408 by the brief's count; about 242 s by arithmetic, about 54 of them at the crossing and about 40 at the table. I have heard none of it, and every score is of the page. MOVES 5. The feeling is made of things that happen to the viewer, and no line of Larry's own asks for it: he asks and then agrees with an answer nobody hears (`how-have-you-been`, the 2.2 s, `yeah-me-too`); our hardest question is said aloud and answered first with `dont-know`; `this-block` is said looking straight ahead and half taken back by the cue `glance`; we are left on the pavement (cue `listen-door`) and he cannot say come up without a book (`q-come-up`, `guest-1`, `guest-2`, `position`); a look, one word and a chair (cue `they-look`, `chair`, cue `chair-in`); and then nobody looks at us (cue `the-meal`). The only lines that tell are the owner's last three, and by then they are earned. INTERESTING 4. Retellable in a sentence, and only this special could hold it. Things planted come back without being pointed at: the lit window twice (cues `stop-at-window`, `apartment-door`); 'guest' three times (`guest-in-sentence`, `guest-2`, `rule`); not eating while someone is outside (`guest-2`, then `late`); a tune nobody finishes, a minute before a sentence about not finishing (`never-ends`, `tarfon-1`). Marked down: the middle is about 54 s at one kerb, and the cut test finds `ruling-stands`. TELEVISION 4. There is something to watch at every moment and the words meet the street in every scene: the cook stopping on the word (cue `cook-slows`) and then 2.4 s of him slow while the room hurries (cue `watch-the-cook`); the busker heard before he is seen (cue `busker-in`); red on Larry through the quotation and still red after it (cue `still-red`); snow with no words (cue `cross`); the door let open from upstairs (cue `let-in`); the camera sitting down (cue `chair-in`); a bowl going past Larry to us with his head following it (cue `served`). Three words on screen. Marked down: six things move by themselves (scarf, coin, door, chair, place setting, bowl), three of them in the last forty seconds; two pictures that carry meaning are very small on a phone (the cook in the hatch; the one figure in the top window at cue `let-in`); the crossing lives on eight changes of shot in one place. LARRY 5. The outline's man. Slower to joke: three light lines of his own in four minutes (`i-looked`, `position`, `my-house`). Personal: `mail-it`, `always-stop`, `used-book`, `this-block`, `started-without-me`, `company`. Never the expert: `zhuangzi-name`, `cook-prince`, `dont-know`, `guest-in-sentence`, `borrow`. Kind: `good-one`. The viewer is talked with five ways: a yes taken (`scarf`), a question asked of us, three questions said back after a turn and a hold of 1.2 to 1.6 s (cues `listen-help`, `listen-put-right`, `listen-door`), and a look answered with nothing repeated (cue `our-look`). The six at the table are themselves in a line each, and nobody says they are friends. IDEAS 5. Three, from three traditions, arriving three ways: seen and told (`cook-hard-part`, `cook-gently`), asked for and borrowed (`tarfon-1`, `tarfon-2`, `dont-finish`, `dont-quit`), and done (`guest-1`, `guest-2`, then the door). Two are things a person could do tonight, the third is done to us, and the busker shows a fourth with no book. They are offered and not displayed: he says where he found the line and that he is a guest in it. Risks, not faults: the central sentence is in the English of 1913 and its plain form comes about ten seconds later; three names the voice will find hard. The attributions read as the cards' safe wordings and the quotation matches its card to the word; that is the auditor's to confirm.
fixedPoints: ok. The five owner's lines are in their places: `no-show`, `paycheck`, `walk-with-me`, then `mixed-up-world` with `keep-close`, and `stay-warm` as the last beat. The table sentence is taken as two beats at its comma (a full stop in the caption, 0.7 s between them) with no cue and no sound beat between the halves; the nearest laugh is Dee's at Sibyl's ruling, about four seconds and a change of shot before it, and it is not on the owner's line. The viewer makes footsteps and nothing else. Each of the three say-backs has a turn and a held gap before it. 'Holidays and all' is the owner's, and the dish is one that nobody names. The sounds are whoosh, tick and murmur; the one laugh is Dee's voiced line. The text on screen is OPEN, DON'T WALK and WALK. We are given a chair, a place and a bowl, and the meal runs from our chair. 408 words by the brief's count (397 spoken, 11 sung), at the floor of the range. Two notes, neither a break: `mail-it` follows the paycheck line and makes it a pretext; and the constitution's credits have to appear somewhere after the last word, which the script leaves to the build.

reasons.reason: first idea the least missed (the emperor)
reasons.note: Cut whole. The first idea is now the cook, and it starts from something he has stopped to look at (`always-stop`, `one-cook`).

They arrive three ways: a picture on the word and then silence; a question, `dont-know`, a quotation and a light that stays red; a reason for something he does, and a door. Each still opens on an old book and two say 'as I remember it', which the accuracy rule asks for. By the third the viewer does see the book coming, and the script uses that: it is how he avoids answering `q-come-up`.
Cut. 2.4 s at cue `watch-the-cook` in its place, and nobody says what it means.
Red for 2.6 s after `dont-quit` (cue `still-red`), then one tick: no chirp, no look up, no remark. The cost is `didnt-arrange`; the lightness after the central sentence is now a tilt of the head.

reasons.reason: the table a welcome party, not a meal
reasons.note: They waited (`late`, clean plates, the gold chair empty); a place is made and a bowl served in front of us; Pete and Hy speak; the bowl and the laugh are Dee's; and then the room forgets us (cue `the-meal`). The meal with nobody attending to the door is 3.2 s before he turns, plus what runs behind his lines and the three seconds after: enough on the page, and the part most at the mercy of staging.
Cut. Nobody states the welcome. Sibyl's one rule is about the order of serving and is used against Larry.
It is now the best-made event in the piece: outside lit glass twice, left on the pavement, `q-come-up`, the couplet as his reason, and the door opened before he can ask.

`mail-it`, `yeah-me-too`, `always-stop`, `used-book`, `this-block` with the cue `glance`, `started-without-me`, `company`. He says where he met one of the three books, and what the walk is to him without naming it.

reasons.reason: `q-all-right` sounds like a figure of speech
reasons.note: Gone. The first say-back is a light question as a beat of its own after a turn and a 1.2 s hold, and before it he asks us something and waits, so the viewer has already been given a silence to speak in. Nothing in the words of `q-does-it-help` marks it as ours; the staging has to.

reasons.reason: the tune's payoff and its captions
reasons.note: No payoff to recognise and no 'la' on the caption line. It stops, starts again behind us, and `never-ends` says what the ear may miss. A viewer without sound sees no singing unless the builder draws it.
Cut. `mail-it` is his own and is not about the show.

`full-house`, the steam grate and `house-record` are gone. The shape `house-record` had (Sibyl's dry line, Eppy calling it like a result, Dee laughing) is back as `ruling-stands` with `dee-laughs`: a fourth beat on the rule where the old one was a second beat on lateness.

joins: `used-book` into `guest-in-sentence`: 'Somebody had already underlined it. He meant the study of Torah.' The two sentences come from different drafts, and on one hearing 'He' is the person who underlined the book, not the rabbi.

`rule` into `my-house` and `still-the-rule`: the exchange was written to answer a rule about waiting that called itself a house rule. Set after 'The guest is served first.' it loses the word it turned on, and Larry now objects to the guest's bowl twenty seconds after quoting a couplet about guests. It can play as the couplet done back to him, which is better than what it was, but it is the one place where the join changes what a line means.
`ruling-stands` with `dee-laughs`: the base's beat on lateness with a new subject, and the only moment at the table that sounds like the show on the air.

Looked at and holding: `what-helped` says 'rattled then, too' although the line that first said 'rattled' was cut, and it now reads as the first naming of what `yeah-me-too` left unsaid. `started-anyway` no longer answers a question and does not need one. The tune's cut payoff leaves no loose end, because `never-ends` closes it on the street.
wouldNotBeMissed: `ruling-stands`: a fourth beat on one rule. `still-the-rule` is already the button, and Dee's laugh lands as well on it.
sendBack: `used-book` into `guest-in-sentence`: on one hearing 'He meant' belongs to the person who underlined the book.
`ruling-stands`: the spare beat from select returned with a new subject, about four seconds before the owner's line. The assembly already puts it to the owner.
`rule` into `my-house`: nothing in the cue `larry-and-sibyl` says how Larry takes it, and the line can be heard as begrudging the guest the bowl.
Cue `let-in`: that the door is opened from upstairs is told only by two ticks and one small figure in a far window. If neither reads on a phone, the door opens by itself.
For the sound editor: `tick` is the lamp, both sets of footsteps, the coin, the sign and the latch. The coin must not sound like a footstep, nor like the note the tune was missing.

notes.json, on length: it names `never-ends` among the first things to cut. That line is the only thing that tells a viewer the tune is unfinished, and the unfinished tune is what the crossing answers.
forTheOwner: A limit to confirm, with the reading in special.md: chapter 9's R10 lists religion as out of bounds even as a reference. At the outline's asking the script names a rabbi and the Torah (`tarfon-who`, `guest-in-sentence`), quotes the Mishnah, and tells from a Daoist classic and a Tamil one. They are treated as special.md asks: he does not joke at them, rank them or speak for them. But special.md's list of what stays out does not mention religion, so this is yours to say.

The last minute, against the show's two endings. Both aired episodes ended with the house taking Larry in after he had put himself outside it, and then turning to the viewer. This would be the third ending with that feeling. I pass it: it is your outline's dinner, done with a chair and a rule, with no music, no lights and no singing. The one line that makes Larry's own part of it rhyme with the other two is `started-without-me`: he counts himself out and `late` counts him in. The assembly offers that line as a choice. Without it, 'Nobody has started.' is news to us and not a correction of him, and the couplet at the door still makes sense.

Two moments stay clear of last week's ending only if they are staged as written. The look and 'Chair.' (cue `they-look`) must not be lit as a stop, with the room dimming and then coming back. The coin (cue `coin`) must not land as the note the tune was missing.

`mail-it` sits between two of your lines and turns 'Just here picking up my paycheck.' into a pretext. I think it is the most personal line in the first minute, and it gives the title. It is still a line that comments on yours.

Your table sentence is two beats with 0.7 s between them and a full stop where you wrote a comma (`mixed-up-world`, `keep-close`), because the voice needs lines of fourteen words or fewer. Dee's laugh at Sibyl's ruling is about four seconds before it.

The crossing is about 54 seconds at one kerb, a little over a fifth of the special, and its central sentence is in the English of 1913 ('thy', 'art thou', 'desist'). The plain version (`dont-finish`, `dont-quit`) comes about ten seconds after the quotation. It is the heart of the piece and the stretch most likely to play long; the writer's own worry says the same.
The light. I would keep it as written: red after he has finished is the street being honest. What it costs is `didnt-arrange`, the line both reviewers liked best at that spot.

The third idea. I would keep the Tamil couplet at the door: it is the one idea that is something he does. The feeling of the Norse line is still there without the poem, in `this-block` and the cue `glance`.

'Keep making things' is shown and not said. Your outline has Larry talk about moving forward and creating. He talks about not quitting; making is carried by a busker who starts with nobody there and never reaches the end (`started-anyway`, `never-ends`) and by one cook feeding a room. I think that is the better choice, and it is yours. It also makes `never-ends` the wrong first cut if length has to come down.

`my-house`. Twenty seconds after telling us you do not eat while a guest stands outside, Larry objects when the guest is served first. Read one way it is his own couplet done back to him and the best laugh at the table; read another he begrudges us the bowl. How he is staged and heard will decide it.

The names. Three that the voice will find hard (Zhuangzi, Tarfon, Tirukkural), carried by the captions under your ruling. He owns up to saying the first one wrong, and says the hardest of the three with no such hedge.
`fast-and-fair` and `q-put-right` carry your context, that justice seems rare. They name nothing, and I read no side in either.

What nobody can judge from the page: four minutes of an earnest Larry in a voice that cannot soften on cue, which is the experiment; whether a say-back with no 'you' in it (`q-does-it-help`) is heard as our question; whether six things moving by themselves read as the show's convention; whether the cook in the hatch and the figure in the top window can be seen on a phone; the busker's own voice.

After the last word. The script ends on a fade with nothing said after 'Goodnight.' The constitution's credits (every voice is synthesized) and the translation's credit still have to appear, and the stock end card is the lit studio with the band and a heading that says good night to Bluesky. That would put a second goodnight after yours and end the special the way both aired episodes ended. It is with the project manager and needs your word.

Small things. 'Oh, no show tonight, folks.' mirrors the first thing Larry ever said on the show ('Oh. Oh no. We're on.'); if that is an accident it is a happy one. The count is at the floor of the range, 397 spoken words and 11 sung syllables, and about 242 seconds before any staging hold is added.
